label: Stand-in: the real item through which a candidate figures in a bearer's favouring
definition: stand b x: the real item through which the candidate x figures in the favouring of the bearer b, so that a real favouring relation of a real bearer has real terms even when the candidate does not exist. For a present input it may be the input itself; for a candidate that is not present it is something else: an abstract candidate or value-fact, an idea, a mode of imitability of the bearer's nature, a power of the bearer directed to x, or the bearer's one undifferentiated nature. Two candidates are individuated in b's favouring when their stand-ins differ. Examples: the idea of a house in an architect deliberating between plans; on Leslie-type axiarchism, the abstract possible world whose ethical requiredness is creatively effective. Non-examples: the candidate itself when it does not exist; a description of the candidate supplied by an observer of the bearer. Structural properties: a declared function of a bearer and a candidate; it need not be injective (the nowhere horn is the constant assignment), and nothing in the type says what kind of item it is or where it is located.
note: Stipulative analyst notion (#2145 premise lane C), attribution deferred. See docs/notes/causal-perfection-transfer.md, section 'Individuating non-present candidates: the axiarchic rival and the cognition criterion'. Lean has no declaration for it: it is the parameter stand : B → X → C of TruthCore.Causality.AxiarchicFoundation, with items typed as C, the content type of the cognition criterion, so that the containment-recognition bridge can say the stand-in itself is the apprehended content.
